finding.title: Watch reactive auth state instead of ref.read-ing currentUser inside _AccountTileState.build()
finding.why: SM-3 requires ref.watch in build and ref.read only in callbacks, precisely because a ref.read snapshot of a mutable getter (`.currentUser`, which changes on sign-in/out/re-auth without the authRepositoryProvider instance itself changing) is only re-evaluated when something else this widget DOES watch happens to force a rebuild — not when the underlying session actually changes. The tile's 'valid session' vs 'sign in again' pill/warning-icon can go stale after an auth event (e.g. a sibling tile's re-auth flow) that doesn't independently invalidate this tile.
finding.recommendation: Replace with a watched, narrow selector, e.g. `ref.watch(authStateProvider.select((s) => s.currentUser?.firebaseUid))`, so the tile is reactive to session changes.
acceptance_criteria: A widget test changes the live Firebase session via a provider override while the picker is mounted and asserts the affected tile's badge updates without an unrelated rebuild trigger

finding.title: Log the comment-only catch blocks that structurally evade the single-line empty-catch grep

evidence.quote:
} catch (e) {
      // Log but don't rethrow — auth deletion + local cleanup still proceed.

} catch (_) {
      // Auth not initialized (tests, or Firebase init failed at

} catch (_) {
        // Network unavailable or CF error — fall through to the default path.

} catch (_) {
        // Silent attempt failed (never shows UI) → fall through to interactive.

finding.why: make audit check 9/15 only matches a literal single-line `catch (_) {}`; each of these 5 blocks contains ONLY a comment across 2-3 lines and no AppLogger call, no rethrow, and no state-producing action, so they are functionally empty and log-less but invisible to the enforced grep. account_management_service.dart's is on the GDPR-style account-deletion path where a comment literally claims 'Log but don't rethrow' yet no logging call exists. The codebase's own convention for the identical 'best-effort cleanup, may throw PlatformException' shape IS to log (see the ~6 AppLogger.warning(event: '..._sign_out_failed', ...) sites already in sign_in_controller.dart), making these omissions an inconsistency, not a deliberate style choice — any of these silent failures is currently undebuggable from production logs.
finding.recommendation: Add `AppLogger.instance.warning(event: '<descriptive_event>', exception: e)` (or `.handle`) to each; consider extending the Makefile's empty-catch grep to strip `//`-comment lines before matching `{\s*}` so this class of gap is caught going forward.
acceptance_criteria: Each of the 5 catch blocks logs via AppLogger
The empty-catch Rule-0 checker is extended to strip comment-only bodies before matching, or a new checker targets this pattern specifically

finding.title: Delete the dead duplicate auth_validators.dart under features/account/onboarding
finding.why: lib/features/account/onboarding/domain/validators/auth_validators.dart is byte-identical (`diff` clean) to lib/features/onboarding/domain/validators/auth_validators.dart, and defines the same public top-level functions (validateEmail, validatePassword, validateDisplayName). A repo-wide grep found zero importers of the features/account copy inside lib/ or test/ — only the features/onboarding copy is actually imported (by signup_screen.dart, sign_in_screen.dart, and 2 tests). Yet account.dart's public barrel re-exports the dead copy as part of the feature's advertised public surface, so any external caller who imports it via the barrel gets a function that is NOT the one this feature's own screens actually use, and a future fix to one copy (e.g. the password-length policy) will silently not apply to the other.
finding.recommendation: Delete lib/features/account/onboarding/domain/validators/auth_validators.dart and its account.dart export line. If validators genuinely need to be shared across features/account and features/onboarding, give them one owning location and have the other import via that feature's barrel.
acceptance_criteria: File removed; account.dart no longer exports it; flutter analyze / build stays green
AG-4 duplicate-symbol grep across lib/ no longer flags validateEmail/validatePassword/validateDisplayName twice

finding.title: Centralize the minimum-password-length constant shared by the UI validator and LocalAuthService
finding.why: The same conceptual policy (minimum local-account password length) is hard-coded as 6 in the client-side form validator and 8 in LocalAuthService's domain-layer check. Today the two never collide end-to-end — the offline-signup path that reaches LocalAuthService.signUp always passes a synthetic UUID password, never the user-typed one gated by the 6-char validator — but the values being a single conceptual invariant with two different numbers is a landmine for the next call site that wires a real user-typed password through both layers (client says valid at 6-7 chars, domain then throws InvalidInputException).
finding.recommendation: Define the constant once (e.g. alongside LocalAuthService or in a small shared constants file) and reference it from auth_validators.dart.
acceptance_criteria: A single named constant is referenced by both the UI validator and LocalAuthService
A unit test asserts the two validators agree at the boundary length

finding.title: Stop interpolating raw exception text into the sign-up failure l10n message
finding.why: This is the exact pattern the repo's (currently broken/non-enforcing per baseline) custom_lint rule `no_e_to_string_in_ui` targets: a raw exception's .toString() is spliced into a user-facing localized string on the local/offline sign-up failure path, so the user can see a technical exception dump instead of translated, actionable copy. It is the only such site in this batch — the other three e.toString() uses in the batch are internal to _extractFirebaseCode's regex parsing and never reach the UI directly.
finding.recommendation: Map the failure to a stable error code (mirroring the existing _mapAuthError switch) and a dedicated generic ARB message instead of interpolating e.toString().
acceptance_criteria: signUpFailed(...) or its replacement no longer receives e.toString()
Once custom_lint is repaired (tracked separately), no_e_to_string_in_ui passes clean on this file
